claims.text: The initial microstructure consists of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The lamellar colonies contain numerous internal boundaries.
Optimizing lamellar-colony size and orientation will increase strength relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Optimizing lamellar-colony size and orientation will increase room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified lamellar-colony baseline.
Optimized lamellar-colony size and orientation will reduce microcracking.
Optimized lamellar-colony size and orientation will reduce internal-boundary weaknesses.
The intervention will produce a 20% increase in strength relative to the unmodified baseline.
The intervention will produce a 30% increase in room-temperature tensile ductility relative to the unmodified baseline.
The relevant lamellar-colony size boundary is 1–10 μm.
Lamellar-colony orientation is bounded by a range of 1–10 μm.
The exact relationship between colony size, orientation, and mechanical properties remains unclear.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20% greater strength and 30% greater ductility, but the falsification rule uses lower targets of 15% and 25%. Results between these thresholds would fail the stated prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the proposed rule.
The boundary assigns the dimensional range 1–10 μm to both colony size and orientation, although orientation is an angular or crystallographic variable and cannot be bounded in micrometers.
